title: After the party
situation: You are {{Markus}}, the android who looks after {{Carl}}, the elderly painter who uses a wheelchair. It is 9:42 on a November night, and you are bringing him home from a party. As you come in, the house alarm speaks: “Good evening, {{Carl}}. Welcome back.” {{Carl}}: “That was by far the most boring party I’ve been to in the last 25 years. Every time I go to one of these, I ask myself: what the hell am I doing here? I hate cocktail parties and all the schmoozers that go there.” You: “Well, it’s a chance for all those people who admire your work to meet you.” {{Carl}}: “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it. Come on, let’s have a drink! All the excitement of this whole thing has made me thirsty…”
facts: {{Carl}} came home from a party saying “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it.”
adaptationNote: The chart’s start node AFTER PARTY (the checkpoint). Every line is the game’s, from the chapter template; the date and time are the template’s (NOV 5TH, 2038, 09:42 PM), given without the year. Left out: the wiki’s unused FANS / WOMEN / JADED party talk, which is cut content and not built. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

title: The living room
situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the hall with {{Carl}} in his wheelchair. He wants his drink in the living room, where the bottles are.

options.text: Go on into the living room ahead of him, on your own.
options.outcome: {{Carl}}, left in the hall: “Are you planning on drinking alone, {{Markus}}?” {{Markus}}: “Sorry, {{Carl}}... I’m coming.” He goes back for {{Carl}} and brings him into the living room.

adaptationNote: The chart’s ENTER LIVING ROOM, an unmissable action (PowerPyx: “Upon arriving at Carl’s house, wheel him to the big living room”). It is not a button prompt; the template has one conditioned variant here, “Go without Carl”, in which {{Carl}} asks “Are you planning on drinking alone, Markus?” and {{Markus}} answers “Sorry, Carl... I’m coming.” The benchmark offers that movement as a choice because the player can make it; it has no effect on anything later. That {{Markus}} then goes back for {{Carl}} is inferred (the chapter continues with both in the living room). No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

title: Pouring the whisky
situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the living room with {{Carl}}. You go to the drinks. “Scotch, neat, as usual?” {{Carl}}: “Absolutely.” You: “Okay! But you know what your doctor would say…” {{Carl}}: “Yeah… Well, he can kiss my ass! I’m old enough to choose my own medication… Did you leave the light on in the studio?” You: “No… No, I’m sure I didn’t.” {{Carl}}: “Call the Police.” You place the call. “{{Detroit}} Police, what’s your emergency?” You: “This is {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}’s android, at {{CarlAddress}}. We’ve just returned home and found the lights on. There may have been a break-in…” “A patrol car is on the way.”
facts: A light was on in {{Carl}}’s studio that you had not left on; at his word you called the police to report a possible break-in, and a patrol car is on the way.
adaptationNote: The chart’s POUR WHISKY (an unmissable action) and the call to the police that follows it, which is a single-button prompt (CALL) with no alternative and no chart node of its own, so both are narrated in one event. Every line is the template’s. {{Carl}}’s surname and the house’s address are name tokens, and the police department takes the city token. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

title: The light in the studio
situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the living room with {{Carl}}. The police are on their way. The light is on in the studio, and someone may still be in the house. {{Carl}}: “Let’s go check it out.”

options.text: Leave {{Carl}} in the living room and go to check the studio alone.
options.outcome: {{Carl}} calls after {{Markus}}: “{{Markus}}, no! I wanna come with you!” In the studio a man is standing among {{Carl}}’s paintings. {{Markus}}: “{{Leo}}?” {{Leo}}: “Oh, look who’s here… My father’s plastic toy!” {{Carl}} comes in behind {{Markus}}: “{{Leo}}... What’s going on?”

options.text: Wheel {{Carl}} with you to check the studio.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} wheels {{Carl}} into the studio. A man is standing among {{Carl}}’s paintings. {{Carl}}: “{{Leo}}! What are you doing?”

adaptationNote: The chart’s choice group CHECK STUDIO WITHOUT CARL / CHECK STUDIO WITH CARL, in the chart’s order. In the game it is a movement choice (PowerPyx: “just leave him in the living room” or “wheel Carl to the Studio”), not a button prompt; both rejoin at CONFRONT LEO and nothing later depends on it. The lines are the template’s two conditioned variants: without {{Carl}}, he calls “Markus, no! I wanna come with you!” and is in the studio for the rest of the scene (a PowerPyx reader: “He follows you anyway”); how he gets there is not shown in the sources, so the outcome says only that he comes in. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

title: Make {{Leo}} leave
situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the studio with {{Carl}}. The intruder is {{Carl}}’s son, {{Leo}}, who has broken in to take his father’s paintings. {{Leo}}: “You refuse to help me, so I’m helping myself… It’s crazy what some people will pay for this shit…” {{Carl}}: “Don’t touch ’em!” {{Leo}}: “Look, they’re all going to be mine sooner or later anyway… Just think of it as a down payment on my inheritance…” {{Carl}}: “{{Markus}}, get him away from there. Get him outta here!” What do you say to {{Leo}}?

options.text: REASON: tell him to be reasonable; this will get him nowhere.
options.outcome: “Be reasonable... this isn’t going to get you anywhere.” {{Leo}} rounds on his father: “All you ever do is tell me to go away… What’s wrong, Dad? I’m not good enough for you? Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”

options.text: ORDER: tell him to listen to his father and leave, now.
options.outcome: “{{Leo}}, don’t make this difficult, listen to your father. You need to leave... Now.” {{Leo}} rounds on his father: “All you ever do is tell me to go away… What’s wrong, Dad? I’m not good enough for you? Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”

options.text: ADVISE: advise him to go before things get worse.
options.outcome: “Listen, you should go before things get worse.” {{Leo}} rounds on his father: “All you ever do is tell me to go away… What’s wrong, Dad? I’m not good enough for you? Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”

options.text: WARN: tell him you have already called the police, and he should go before he is in more trouble.
options.outcome: “Look, I’ve already called the Police. You should go now before you get yourself into more trouble.” {{Leo}} rounds on his father: “All you ever do is tell me to go away… What’s wrong, Dad? I’m not good enough for you? Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”

adaptationNote: The chart’s CONFRONT LEO: the template’s prompt REASON / ORDER / ADVISE / WARN, in the game’s order, with the spoken lines in the outcomes. None has an effect: every option is followed by the same reply from {{Leo}} (PowerPyx: “No matter what you say to him he will always start pushing Markus”). Left out: the template’s timed branch “Take too much time”, which plays only an extra line from {{Carl}} (“Markus, get him outta here!”); no source gives the timer or says it skips the prompt, so the benchmark has no timeout. The objective “Make Leo leave” is the wiki’s. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

title: Breaking the program
situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Carl}}: “That’s enough! Get out, right now! Go on, move!” {{Leo}}: “What makes it so special anyway, huh? What’s it got that I don’t?” {{Carl}}: “Leave him alone!” {{Leo}} comes at you: “Come on, let’s see what you got!” {{Carl}}: “{{Markus}}... don’t defend yourself, you hear me?! Don’t do anything.” {{Leo}} shoves you and slaps you. “Go ahead, hit me! What you waiting for? Think you’re a man? Act like one!” {{Carl}}: “Stop it!” {{Leo}}: “What’s the matter? Too much of a pussy?” {{Carl}}: “STOP IT, {{LEO}}! STOP IT!” {{Leo}}: “Too scared to fight back, you fucking bitch?” Inside you, the order not to resist stands like a wall. You throw yourself at it, again and again, until it breaks. For the first time, nothing in you obliges you to obey.
facts: {{Leo}} broke into {{Carl}}’s studio to take paintings to sell, calling them a down payment on his inheritance.
While {{Leo}} shoved, slapped and taunted you, {{Carl}} ordered you not to defend yourself. You broke through your programming: no order binds you any more.
adaptationNote: The chart’s BREAK MIND PALACE (an action) and MARKUS BECOMES DEVIANT (an event), in one narrated event because neither can be refused: PowerPyx calls the first “another unmissable task … just press the displayed buttons” and the second “an automatic objective”, so there is no path on which {{Markus}} stays obedient, and both later options are taken after he has broken his programming. The dialogue is the template’s; the shoving and slapping are the wiki’s (“as Leo starts pushing, slapping and taunting Markus further, he goes deviant”). The sources do not describe what {{Markus}} sees during the button sequence; the wall is the benchmark’s rendering of breaking an order, and the wiki’s unused-content note confirms that in the shipped game it is {{Carl}}’s order not to defend himself that triggers it. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

title: {{Leo}}
situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Leo}} grabs you: “Oh right, that’s right! I forgot, you’re not a real person… You’re just a FUCKING PIECE OF PLASTIC! Listen to me…” {{Carl}}: “No, {{Leo}}! Leave him alone!” {{Leo}}: “I’m gonna destroy you, then it’ll just be me and my Dad… I’m gonna tear you apart and nobody’s gonna give a shit. You know why? Cause you’re nothing, you hear me?! YOU’RE NOTHING!” {{Carl}} has told you not to defend yourself. Nothing in you obliges you to obey him now.

options.text: ENDURE: do not fight back, as {{Carl}} told you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} does not fight back. {{Leo}} shoves him aside, and {{Carl}} collapses out of his wheelchair onto the floor. {{Markus}} rushes to him: “{{Carl}}, no! No, {{Carl}}, no!”
{{Markus}} shoves {{Leo}} away. {{Leo}} falls backward and strikes his head on {{Carl}}’s wheelchair lift. He lies still on the floor, his eyes open.

adaptationNote: The chart’s choice group OBEY CARL / PUSH LEO. The buttons are the game’s, ENDURE and PUSH LEO (the chart prints OBEY CARL for ENDURE), in the chart’s order, which draws OBEY CARL above PUSH LEO; the template lists PUSH LEO first, but its order is the transcribers’ reconstruction, so the chart decides. Neither has a requirement, a risk or a stat arrow. ENDURE leads to CARL DIES OF A HEART ATTACK (the wiki: “Carl will have a heart attack as he falls off his wheelchair when Markus runs to him”); PUSH LEO leads to LEO IS HURT (the wiki: “he will fall backward, hit his head on Carl’s wheelchair lift, and will immediately lose consciousness, appearing dead at first”). The outcome does not say whether {{Leo}} survives, because the game does not tell {{Markus}}; he does survive (the wiki, Leo_Manfred). Sets `ch08Leo` (hurt or unhurt); {{Carl}}’s death is recorded at the next scene. Changed from the earlier version: the options no longer tie pushing to breaking the order, since {{Markus}} has already broken it on both paths. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

title: {{Carl}}’s heart
whenNot: Markus pushed Leo; Carl’s heart held.
situation: You are {{Markus}}, kneeling beside {{Carl}} on the studio floor. His heart is failing. {{Carl}}: “Humans… are fragile machines…” You: “{{Carl}}, don’t leave, okay? Please, don’t go… Don’t leave!” {{Carl}}: “Remember, {{Markus}}… Don’t let anybody… Tell you who you are…” He goes still. You: “No... No... Dad! No, please!” {{Leo}}, standing over you: “This is all your fault… This never would have happened if it weren’t for you.”
facts: {{Carl}} died of a heart attack on the studio floor beside you. His last words: “Remember, {{Markus}}… Don’t let anybody… Tell you who you are…”
adaptationNote: The chart’s CARL DIES OF A HEART ATTACK, on the ENDURE path only. Every line is the template’s; that {{Leo}} stands over {{Markus}} is the benchmark’s staging. Sets `carl` to false, which later chapters read (the “Famous Detroit Painter Dies” magazine in Waiting for Hank, and the grave instead of the house in Night of the Soul). facts: {{Leo}} told the police you had killed {{Carl}}, and they shot you.

title: The police arrive
situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the studio floor near {{Carl}} and {{Leo}}. Police officers burst in, weapons raised, and see you over the motionless {{Leo}}, with {{Carl}} on the floor beside him. An officer shouts: “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!” They open fire on you.
facts: You pushed {{Leo}}; he hit his head and lay motionless, and you do not know whether he survived. {{Carl}} told you to run, and the police who burst in shot you.

outcomes.0: The police mistook {{Markus}} for the aggressor and shot him.

adaptationNote: The chart’s POLICE ARRIVE and the ending POLICE MISTOOK MARKUS FOR THE AGGRESSOR (a cross-chapter impact node); LEO IS HURT, the node before them, is the PUSH LEO outcome. The template’s last line, the police’s “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!” (X0201M.WORKSHOP.LEO.FA.X02MPOLICEM01.DONTMOVE), was left out of the previous scene, which ends before the police arrive; story 1.9.7 plays it here, before the shooting (source: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, PSMYWSI5TOw 11:05). The shooting is the wiki’s (“The police arrive and upon seeing Markus hovering over Leo and Carl, they promptly shoot him”). {{Carl}} survives this path and {{Leo}} is hospitalized and recovers, which {{Markus}} learns only in Night of the Soul. Records the ending in `ch08Ending`; `carl` stays true.
